# R163 WS3, re-measured: the chapter's two programs (chapter 19 section 2; the same sources as peak-memory.txt)
# Sutram 1.0 (v315) - sampurna sutra, Linux (kernel build redacted), /usr/bin/time -f %M (KB), 2026-11-09
# blk.bin de31c1363bb824ec  noblk.bin b977fbd12c545b1c  (the same binaries as peak-memory.txt)

## 1. started with an empty environment: env -i /usr/bin/time -f %M ./X.bin   (75 runs each; output, KB)
blk.bin:  75 264;
noblk.bin:  75 49920;

## 2. started from this session's shell (environment 20799 bytes): /usr/bin/time -f %M ./X.bin   (75 runs each)
blk.bin:  57 264; 18 392;
noblk.bin:  1 49792; 74 49920;

## 3. blk.bin, the environment's size (30 runs each)
env -i:  30 264;
env plus one 100,000-byte variable:  8 476; 21 480; 1 564;

## 4. the earlier record (peak-memory.txt, an earlier shell in this session): blk 55 runs: 19 x 308, 36 x 436; noblk 55 x 49920

Reading: without the block the peak is the 200,000 buffers (51,200,000 bytes) and is 49,920 KB (74 of 75 from
the shell, once 49,792). With the block it is a few hundred KB and depends on how the program is started: 264 KB
every time with an empty environment; 264, 308, 392 or 436 KB from a shell; 476-564 KB with a 100 KB variable.
The chapter's 392 (R157) and R163's first '308 or 436 in 75 runs' (55 runs were recorded, not 75) were each one
shell's figure. The chapter now gives 264 KB with env -i (75 of 75), 264-436 KB from a shell, and 49,920 KB.
